content: 1. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of triazolam by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Rifampin decreases the plasma levels or efficacy of trimethoprim by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised, and caution should be exercised. 3. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of trimipramine through its impact on CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 4. Trofinetide increases the plasma levels or effects of rifampin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Trofinetide, as an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, may elevate plasma levels of substrates of these transporters. Avoid coadministration with sensitive substrates. 5. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of rifampin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are required. Conversely, rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tucatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Tucatinib, a CYP2C8 substrate, has reduced plasma concentrations when coadministered with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inducers. 6. Rifampin reduces the levels of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ulipristal by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Use an alternative drug if necessary. 10. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of vadadustat through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. OAT1/OAT3 inhibitors may increase vadadustat AUC, necessitating close monitoring for excessive or rapid hemoglobin response and potential adverse reactions. 11. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of valbenazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Rifampin and valoctocogene roxaparvovec both increase plasma levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. Medications with hepatotoxic potential may increase the risk of elevated liver enzymes when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec. Consider alternative medications and monitor closely for drug interactions. 13. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of valsartan through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Valsartan is a substrate of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1, and coadministration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 14. Rifampin reduces the levels of vandetanib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Avoid coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inducers, as they reduce vandetanib exposure by up to 40%. 15. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Vemurafenib increases the levels of rifampin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, while rifampin decreases vemurafenib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of venetoclax by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers. Consider alternative treatments with less CYP3A induction. 19. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of verapamil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Rifampin reduces the levels of vilazodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider increasing the vilazodone dose up to twofold (not exceeding 80 mg/day) when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers for more than 14 days. Reduce the dose to the original level within 14 days after discontinuing the inducer. 21. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are required. 22. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of vincristine and vincristine liposomal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 23. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 24. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Rifampin decreases the levels of vorapaxar by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Rifampin reduces the levels of voriconazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Voriconazole also decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. 27. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vortioxetine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider increasing the vortioxetine dose (not exceeding three times the original dose) when coadministered with strong CYP inducers for more than 14 days. Reduce the dose to the original level within 14 days after discontinuing the inducer. 28. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Avoid coadministration of voxilaprevir and rifampin. 29. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of warfarin by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of zaleplon by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 31. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 32. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of intranasal zavegepant through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. OATP1B3 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to zavegepant. 33. Rifampin reduces the levels of zidovudine by inducing metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 34. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 35. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of zolpidem by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 36. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of zuranolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Rifampin is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to isoniazid or rifamycins, acute liver disease, severe hepatic damage, or acute gout. It is also contraindicated in patients receiving ritonavir-boosted saquinavir due to an increased risk of severe hepatocellular toxicity. 39. Rifampin is contraindicated with many drugs that are CYP substrates, particularly CYP3A4. Coadministration with atazanavir, darunavir, fosamprenavir, saquinavir, or tipranavir may substantially decrease plasma concentrations, leading to loss of antiviral efficacy for HIV and/or development of viral resistance. 40. Rifampin may complicate diabetes management and is not recommended for intermittent therapy. Patients should be cautioned against interruptions in daily dosing, as rare renal hypersensitivity reactions have been reported upon resumption of therapy. 41. Rifampin induces enzymes that enhance the metabolism of endogenous substrates, including adrenal hormones, thyroid hormones, and vitamin D. 42. Rifampin crosses the placental barrier and appears in cord blood. When administered during the last weeks of pregnancy, it may cause postnatal hemorrhages in the mother and infant, which may require vitamin K treatment. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. 43. Rifampin has shown tumorigenic potential in animal studies. A decision should be made to discontinue nursing or the drug, considering the importance of the drug to the mother. 44. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk, and rifampin is generally considered acceptable in such cases.
